TextView.android:text: Lesson 1 - Unit 4: Sa, Kay, Kina, and Everyday Words
is a preposition that can mean
I am studying at University of California.
I will go to California tomorrow.
She/he gave the food to her/his friend.
beneficiary of an action or object.
I will buy food for my mom.
I will cook for my spouse (wife/husband).
I will clean the house for my visitor.
We will celebrate Ella's birthday on April 8.
I will go to Texas in December.
I will go on vacation in __(day/month/date/season)__.
When 'Sa' comes before a pronoun that starts with a vowel, drop the first vowel and replace it with 'Sa'.
Additionally, if a word ends in a vowel and the next one begins with a vowel, they can sometimes be combined.
Used instead of 'Sa' when talking about people's names.
- for more than one person's names.
I will buy food for Lisa.
I will cook for Lisa and Aaron.
Bibili ako ng regalo para kay _____.
I will buy a gift for _____.
Magluluto ako ng adobo para kay _____.
I will go shopping for ____ and ____.
Saan ka pupunta pagkatapos ng klase?
Where will you go after class?
Pupunta ako sa _____ pagkatapos ng klase.
I will go to _____ after class.
